instruction: Hide columns E through H in this spreadsheet so only the first date's attendance data is visible, then save the file.

command: import pyautogui; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); import time; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully resized cells in the spreadsheet to fit on one page and exported to PDF. Used Format > Page Style to adjust scaling, then exported via File > Export as PDF.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc menus, adjust page style settings, select cells/columns, use Format menu options, and save files.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests column manipulation in the same spreadsheet. The original task involved page layout; this variation tests column visibility control.
metadata.explanation: Task requires hiding columns E-H to show only the first date section. Evaluator checks that columns E, F, G, H are all marked as hidden in the saved xlsx file.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses openpyxl column_dimensions[col].hidden to check column visibility for E, F, G, H — the exact columns specified in the instruction.
Metric correctly receives the rules dict directly (expected.type='rule') and accesses expected.get('expected_hidden', {}) without wrapping errors.
Data flow is correct: getter returns {'hidden_status': {col: bool}} and metric reads result.get('hidden_status', {}) to compare against expected values.
Postconfig ensures file is saved (Ctrl+S) before getter reads from disk, preventing stale state issues.
Full coverage: both instruction requirements are verified — column hiding (getter/metric) and file saving (postconfig ensures save, getter reads saved file).
Partial credit scoring (0.25 per column) is sensible for a 4-column verification task.
